title: appbuilder-mvp cannot pass its own hard gates (stories.yaml, 07_screens)
detail: `spec-featuresets` hard-gates `_concept/04_journeys/stories.yaml`, but the flow has no `experience-journeys` node. `build-plan` and `build-implement` hard-gate `_concept/07_screens`, but the flow has no `spec-feature` or `experience-shell` node. title: appbuilder-standard runs mockup-storybook before the tech stack it hard-gates on
detail: `mockup-storybook` hard-gates `10_blueprint/techstack.md` and reads it in step 1. In `appbuilder-standard` it runs at node 12; `architecture-techstack` runs at node 15, after annotate and feedback. The gate cannot be open when the node starts.
recommendation: Move `architecture-techstack` and `architecture-system` before the mockup nodes. Or gate `mockup-storybook` soft and take the framework from the template default.

title: skaileup-concept-reverse runs spec-feature; nothing writes its scope.yaml gate
detail: `spec-feature` hard-gates `_concept/01_meta/scope.yaml`. The reverse flow starts at `concept-reverse`, which only reads that file, and has no `concept-scope` node. When the host's profile picker starts the flow, no node writes `scope.yaml`. A grep of `skaile-forge/server` for `scope.yaml` and `01_meta` finds 0 hits, so the host writes none either.

evidence.quote: started the run from an onboarding profile

recommendation: Make `concept-scope` the entry of the reverse flow, or let `concept-reverse` write `scope.yaml` with `flow: skaileup-concept-reverse`.

title: check.py never checks that a hard gate has an upstream writer
detail: The docstring says a prerequisite no skill writes is raised here. `_check_one_flow` (lines 730-842) checks id, name, presentation, node ids, edge types, reachability and `requires:`. It never compares a node's hard gate with the nodes upstream, so F01 to F03 stay green. A search of check.py for writer or producer logic finds none.

evidence.quote: prerequisite path that no skill writes is a gate that can never open

recommendation: Add a rule: walk each flow's `type: flow` edges, collect the targets written so far, and fail on a hard gate with no writer upstream. It needs the `produces` list of F05.

title: No skill declares what it produces, so the editor cannot derive done state
detail: The editor marks a node done from `contracts/artifacts.yaml` `produced_by`, and falls back to the session when none exists. This collection ships no such file: ADR 0001 records it as unreachable under a copy install, and no skill frontmatter has a `produces` key. `skaileup` step 3.2 therefore walks the tree for the first node whose artifacts are missing, with no list to look up.

The first node whose artifacts are not yet in the tree

recommendation: Add `metadata.artifacts.produces: [{id, path}]` to every skill, checked by check.py. Ask the host to read done state from that list, as it already reads `artifacts.requires`.
